title: Two Sum (Sorted)
description: Given a sorted array of numbers and a target, return the indices [i, j] of the two numbers that add up to the target. Exactly one solution exists.
whatShouldHappen: Place a left pointer at index 0 and a right pointer at the last index.
While left < right, check the sum of the two pointed elements.
If the sum equals the target, return [left, right].
If the sum is too small, move the left pointer right. If too large, move the right pointer left.
patternExplanation: Start pointers at opposite ends and move them toward each other based on whether the current sum is too small or too large — exploits sorted order to avoid O(n²) brute force.

title: Remove Duplicates In-Place
description: Given a sorted array, remove duplicates in-place so each value appears only once. Return the count of unique elements. The first k elements of the array should hold the unique values.
whatShouldHappen: Use a slow pointer to track where the next unique value should go.
Use a fast pointer to scan every element.
When the fast pointer finds a value different from the slow pointer's value, advance the slow pointer and write the new value there.
Return the slow pointer + 1 as the count of unique elements.
patternExplanation: A slow pointer marks where to write; a fast pointer reads ahead. When fast finds something new, slow advances and the value is written there — modifies the array in O(1) extra space.

title: Valid Palindrome
description: Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome, or false otherwise. A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize left pointer at 0 and right pointer at s.length - 1.
Skip any non-alphanumeric characters on either side.
Compare characters in lowercase. If they don't match, return false.
Advance left and decrement right until they meet. If all match, return true.

traceTable.inputLabel: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
tests.label: standard palindrome with punctuation

input: Was it a car or a cat I saw?
tests.label: complex palindrome

patternExplanation: Move pointers from both ends inward, skipping non-alphanumeric chars and checking equality in O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Container With Most Water
description: You are given an integer array height of length n. There are n vertical lines drawn such that the two endpoints of the ith line are (i, 0) and (i, height[i]). Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container that stores the most water. Return the maximum amount of water a container can store.
whatShouldHappen: Start with left pointer at 0 and right pointer at height.length - 1.
Calculate current area: width * min(height[left], height[right]).
Update maximum area found so far.
Move the pointer pointing to the shorter vertical line inward to try finding a taller line.
Repeat until left and right meet, then return maxArea.
patternExplanation: Always advance the pointer with smaller height because keeping the shorter line can never produce a larger area with smaller width.

title: Move Zeroes
description: Given an integer array nums, move all 0's to the end of it while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements. You must do this in-place and return the modified array.
whatShouldHappen: Use a write pointer starting at index 0.
Iterate through nums with a read pointer.
When nums[read] is non-zero, swap nums[write] with nums[read] and increment write.
Return the modified nums array.
patternExplanation: A slow write pointer marks the boundary of non-zero elements while a fast read pointer finds non-zeros to swap forward.

title: Squares of a Sorted Array
description: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array of the squares of each number sorted in non-decreasing order in O(n) time.
whatShouldHappen: Allocate a result array of the same length.
Initialize left at 0 and right at nums.length - 1.
Place a pointer p at the end of the result array.
Compare the square of nums[left] and nums[right].
Put the larger square at result[p] and decrement p while moving that pointer inward.
patternExplanation: Since the largest squares must originate from the outer ends (large negative or large positive), compare ends and populate from back to front in O(n).

title: Reverse String In-Place
description: Write a function that reverses an array of characters in-place using two pointers. Return the modified array.
whatShouldHappen: Set left pointer to 0 and right pointer to s.length - 1.
Swap characters at s[left] and s[right].
Advance left by 1 and decrement right by 1.
Stop when left >= right and return s.
patternExplanation: Swapping elements from both boundaries moving inward reverses the entire sequence in O(n/2) steps with O(1) space.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize left = 0, right = height.length - 1, leftMax = 0, rightMax = 0, water = 0.
While left < right, compare height[left] with height[right].
If height[left] < height[right], update leftMax. If height[left] < leftMax, add leftMax - height[left] to water; then advance left++.
Otherwise, update rightMax. If height[right] < rightMax, add rightMax - height[right] to water; then decrement right--.
Return total trapped water.
patternExplanation: Using two pointers moving inward from both ends allows computing water trapped based on the smaller bounded boundary in O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Sort Colors (Dutch National Flag)
description: Given an array nums with n objects colored red (0), white (1), or blue (2), sort them in-place so that objects of the same color are adjacent, in order 0, 1, and 2.
whatShouldHappen: Use three pointers: low = 0 (boundary for 0s), mid = 0 (current element), high = nums.length - 1 (boundary for 2s).
While mid <= high, check nums[mid].
If nums[mid] === 0, swap nums[low] and nums[mid], increment low++ and mid++.
If nums[mid] === 1, just increment mid++.
If nums[mid] === 2, swap nums[mid] and nums[high], decrement high-- (do not advance mid yet).
Return the sorted array nums in-place.
patternExplanation: Dijkstra Dutch National Flag algorithm partitions an array into three segments in a single pass O(n) and O(1) space.

title: 3Sum Closest
description: Given an integer array nums of length n and an integer target, find three integers in nums such that the sum is closest to target. Return the sum of the three integers.
whatShouldHappen: Sort nums in ascending order.
Initialize closestSum to nums[0] + nums[1] + nums[2].
Iterate i from 0 to nums.length - 3.
For each i, set left = i + 1, right = nums.length - 1.
Compute sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right].
If Math.abs(target - sum) < Math.abs(target - closestSum), update closestSum = sum.
If sum < target, advance left++; if sum > target, decrement right--; if sum === target, return sum directly.
patternExplanation: Sorting the array enables directional two-pointer traversal inside an outer loop, reducing an O(n^3) search to O(n^2).

title: Backspace String Compare
description: Given two strings s and t, return true if they are equal when both are typed into empty text editors. "#" means a backspace character. Resolve in O(1) space.
whatShouldHappen: Iterate backwards through both strings using two pointers i = s.length - 1, j = t.length - 1.
Maintain skip count for each string when "#" is encountered.
Skip deleted characters until reaching valid characters to compare.
If both valid characters match, decrement both pointers and continue.
If one string has a valid character and the other does not, return false.
Return true if both pointers successfully process all characters.
patternExplanation: Iterating backward from string ends handles backspaces naturally in O(1) auxiliary space without building stack strings.
